messages.author: Rachael Jack
messages.title: Open-Rank Faculty Positions in Computational Mind & Behavior | Vanderbilt University
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues

We're hiring at Vanderbilt!  Join us in building Computational Mind & Behavior.

We use computation to make mind and behavior explainable—and mind and behavior to make new forms of computation possible.

At Vanderbilt University's College of Connected Computing, we're building Computational Mind & Behavior (CMB) around this two-way scientific ambition. We're recruiting exceptional scholars at Assistant, Associate, and Full Professor levels to help shape our scientific directions, collaborations, and intellectual community.

Our vision is to discover the principles that generate intelligence and behavior—from brains and individuals to interacting agents, groups, cultures, and societies—and understand what happens as human and artificial intelligence become increasingly intertwined.

We're particularly interested in four interconnected research directions:
🧠 Brain & Cognition / NeuroAI — How biological and artificial systems perceive, learn, reason, decide, and adapt.
💬 Language, Embodiment & Interaction — How minds communicate and connect through language, multimodal signals, embodied behavior, and human–AI interaction.
🤝 Strategic Social Behavior — How cooperation, competition, social inference, and strategic decision-making emerge among interacting agents.
🌐 Networks & Collective Intelligence — How behavior and intelligence emerge across social networks, cultures, populations, and human–AI collectives.

We welcome outstanding researchers from computing, AI, psychology, cognitive science, neuroscience, and related disciplines. We value deep disciplinary expertise, ambitious scientific questions, innovative computational approaches, and the potential to forge new connections across fields.

Join us in building an intellectual community that connects fundamental discoveries about intelligence and behavior with new computational ideas, methods, and technologies.

Interested in joining us?
We'd be delighted to hear from prospective candidates and discuss our scientific vision, recruitment priorities, and opportunities within CMB.

Contact
Prof. Rachael E. Jack
Area Head, Computational Mind & Behavior
EMAIL_REDACTED

How to apply
Application links:
Assistant Professor: https://lnkd.in/eWVhNVtY
Associate & Full Professor: https://lnkd.in/edtYbiym

In Interfolio, select “Humans, Computing and Society” as your primary review area; identify a secondary review area, if applicable (e.g., Physical Intelligence). In your cover letter, explicitly state your interest in Computational Mind & Behavior (CMB).

Explore our scientific vision: https://lnkd.in/eW3YVmev

Full consideration deadline: December 1, 2026.

Please share widely with colleagues and potential candidates!


Prof. Rachael E. Jack, Ph.D.
Professor of Computational Social Cognition
Professor of Psychology
Area Lead: Computational Mind & Behavior
Co-Director: MOSAIC
Past-President | Society for Affective Science
Editor-in-Chief | Advances in Psychological Science Open
College of Connected Computing
Vanderbilt University
Nashville, Tennessee, USA

messages.author: Daniel Bush
messages.title: Single Unit Studies of Human Intelligence (SUSHI) Symposium 2027
messages.body_html:
Dear Colleagues,

We wish to invite you to attend the SUSHI (Single Unit Studies of Human Intelligence) symposium, a two-day satellite event taking place in Glasgow immediately before the 7th International Conference on Memory (ICOM-7) next year.

SUSHI will bring together leading laboratories using human intracranial single-neuron recordings to investigate learning, memory, and higher-order cognition. The symposium is intended as a focused forum for discussing recent advances, emerging methods, and future directions in the study of human single-neuron activity.

The programme will consist exclusively of short talks from leading researchers in the field, designed to maximise scientific exchange and discussion.

The symposium will be organised around two broad themes:
Day 1 - Episodic memory, spatial cognition, and the hippocampus
Day 2 - Speech and language, auditory cognition, and the neocortex

For those interested in only one of these themes, single-day registration options will be available.

We hope that SUSHI will provide a unique opportunity for researchers working with human single-unit recordings to exchange ideas in an intimate setting before joining the broader memory science community at ICOM-7.

Further details, including registration information and the scientific programme, can be found on the symposium website here. You can sign up to receive further updates via the mailing list here.

We would be delighted if you could join us in Glasgow, and grateful if you could share this invitation with any interested parties.

With best wishes,

Daniel Bush & Simon Hanslmayr
On behalf of the SUSHI 2027 Organising Committee

----------------------------------------------------

Dr. Daniel Bush

GM01, Medical Sciences Building, Gower Street, London, WC1E 6BT

Associate Professor, UCL Department of Neuroscience, Physiology and Pharmacology

Principal Investigator, UCL Human Electrophysiology Lab

Co-director, UCL Centre for Neuro-AI

Section Editor, PLoS Computational Biology

messages.title: Open Rank Faculty Position in Basic Biomedical Research – WashU Medicine
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues,

The Division of Basic Research in the Department of Anesthesiology at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis is recruiting tenure track or tenured faculty.

Our open rank search welcomes outstanding scientists across all areas of basic biomedical research, including molecular and cellular biology, neuroscience, and related disciplines. We seek creative and innovative investigators who will bring new scientific directions and help shape the future of basic research in our highly collaborative environment. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

For additional information and to apply:
https://facultyopportunities.wustl.edu/Posting/Detail/1011265

Please share this opportunity with interested colleagues and trainees.

Thank you!
Wayland Cheng             
                                                                               
Wayland Cheng, MD PhD
Associate Professor
Department of Anesthesiology
Washington University in St. Louis, School of Medicine
